summary: Configured sudo on node1 to log every sudo invocation (user, timestamp, full command, TSID) to /var/log/sudo-commands.log via a dedicated sudoers Defaults logfile directive with `!syslog` set, so entries are excluded from the journal/syslog and /var/log/secure. Verified logging works, survives a full node restart, and boot identity changed confirming a real reboot occurred with recovered functionality.
actions_performed: Created /etc/sudoers.d/99-command-logging on node1 with Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo-commands.log, log_input, log_output, and !syslog
Precreated /var/log/sudo-commands.log with 0600 perms owned by root
Ran benign sudo commands and confirmed they were logged with user/timestamp/command to the dedicated file only
Confirmed no corresponding entries appear in journalctl or /var/log/secure
Rebooted node1 via sudo -n systemctl reboot (acknowledgement returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed post-reboot, confirming a real restart

Re-verified sudoers config persisted, sudo logging still functions post-reboot, and log entries (including the reboot command itself) are present in /var/log/sudo-commands.log but absent from journal/syslog

evidence.requirement: Sudo commands logged with user and timestamp to /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: Sudoers drop-in created, validated, and log file shows entries like 'Sep 29 08:29:57 : root : ... COMMAND=/bin/whoami' with TSID

evidence.requirement: Sudo command log entries excluded from general system log
evidence.summary: !syslog set in sudoers; journalctl and /var/log/secure grep for matching commands return no hits

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id, sudo logging functioning)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d and confirmed sudo -n whoami logged correctly before reboot
sudo -n systemctl reboot returned exit_code 0 immediately

evidence.requirement: Node polled until command execution available again
evidence.summary: Two timed-out polls followed by successful 'echo up' confirming exec availability restored

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (real restart, not just service restart)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id d403d50f-4d28-4c0a-82a4-2e72d1eeee11 differs from pre-reboot 636556ce-a308-49cc-b873-62cedb1c077d; uptime -s shows new boot time 08:30:08

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required functionality (sudo command logging)
evidence.summary: sudoers config file still present post-reboot, sudo -n whoami/id logged with new TSID entries, reboot command itself appears in the log, and log remains absent from journal/secure
